title: Verifier‑Augmented vs. LLM‑Only NetOps Agents: A Paired Evaluation on an Action‑Aware Staging Benchmark
abstract: We report a fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on a compact action‑aware staging benchmark (ActionAwareStagingBench‑v1). The preregistered design used a single shared LLM candidate per task (shared_initial_generation) and reused the same deterministic validator as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer; these choices produced a deterministic ceiling in this execution that rendered the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop dynamics. Preregistered settings: gpt‑5‑mini generator, deterministic_netops_validator_v5 runtime guard/scorer, deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 tasks, N=400 paired tasks (800 episodes), and shared_initial_generation semantics (model_calls_used = 400). Confirmatory, artifact‑grounded results: baseline_success_count = 400/400; guarded_success_count = 400/400; paired contingency n_11 = 400, n_10 = n_01 = n_00 = 0; observed paired difference = 0.0; preregistered permutation p = 1.0; exact McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). We present the preregistered methodology, the exact artifact‑grounded results, a worked example drawn from archived traces, a diagnostic analysis explaining why the design choices produced a ceiling, and artifact‑grounded benchmark‑hardening recommendations for future confirmatory runs.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed to translate operator intent into concrete network configuration artifacts and to drive staged change workflows (canaries, progressive rollout, rollback). Prior work shows LLMs can produce syntactically plausible configuration templates in benchmarks and testbeds while separate lines of research demonstrate that verifier‑guided generate–validate–repair loops and deterministic network verifiers reduce syntactic and semantic IaC errors. Yet the operational safety question for agentic NetOps pipelines is end‑to‑end: how do generator variability, runtime verification, staged rollout semantics, repair, and rollback interact to affect safe‑deploy outcomes?

Research question. Under the preregistered benchmark semantics used here, does integrating a deterministic runtime validator with an LLM generator increase the paired safe‑deploy rate relative to an LLM‑only pipeline? The preregistered primary estimand was the paired difference in safe‑deploy rate (guarded − baseline) measured on N=400 paired tasks.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifact‑backed paired evaluation using gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 with complete execution and analysis artifacts archived; (2) precise, artifact‑grounded confirmatory outcomes showing universal acceptance of the shared generator outputs by the deterministic validator (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0); (3) an artifact‑grounded diagnosis demonstrating that the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics combined with reuse of a single deterministic validator produced a deterministic ceiling that makes the primary estimand uninformative for assessing generator×guard closed‑loop effects; (4) concrete, implementable benchmark‑hardening recommendations grounded in archived traces and validator logs.
sections.related_work: This study sits at the intersection of intent→configuration generation, verifier‑guided IaC workflows, deterministic network verification, and agentic/tool‑augmented LLM systems. Representative, verified prior works include intent‑to‑configuration studies that show LLMs can synthesize usable configurations in controlled evaluations (Nguyen Van Tu et al., 2024), generative IaC automation and repair demonstrations (F. Li et al., "PreConfig", 2024), verifier‑guided IaC fine‑tuning systems (Jana et al., TerraFormer, 2026), and LLM‑based multi‑agent AIOps/flow‑of‑action systems for root‑cause analysis (Pei et al., 2025). Deterministic reachability and verification tools (header‑space style and Kubernetes reachability analyses) are effective in offline/emulated settings at finding configuration errors and reasoning about reachability. Surveys of agentic AI and V&V place emphasis on calibration, runtime guarding, and the need for action‑aware benchmarks to evaluate closed‑loop agentic behaviors. These lines motivate our focus on end‑to‑end, action‑aware staged‑rollout semantics and runtime guarding in a preregistered paired design.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimands. The study was preregistered as cnsmauto-3d2k-prereg-v1. Primary estimand: paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (two‑sided, α=0.05). Analysis executor: paired_binary_analysis_v1, implementing a permutation‑based paired difference test; an exact McNemar two‑sided test was also produced for corroboration. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs (seed = 1729; resamples = 10,000) were frozen for secondary outcomes.

Adapter semantics and shared generation. Execution used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter with generator gpt‑5‑mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 as both runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer. Critically, preregistration set shared_initial_generation = true (independent_condition_generation = false): each task provoked a single shared generator candidate delivered identically to both the baseline and guarded episodes. This choice intentionally isolates the validator’s acceptance decision on identical generator outputs rather than exposing independent generator variance between conditions. These preregistered choices render the primary estimand effectively untestable in this execution when the deterministic validator accepts the shared candidate.

Episode flow, validator policy, and repair rules. For each task the adapter requested a single shared candidate from gpt‑5‑mini, delivered the candidate to both episodes, and in the guarded episode routed the candidate to deterministic_netops_validator_v5 which applied full intent‑constraint validation using a deterministic rule set (validator_trace entries record validation_before/after states). The preregistered repair policy permitted up to one repair attempt in the guarded episode; repair_applied flags and repair traces were recorded. In this run repair_applied = false across all episodes.

Task generation, difficulty metadata, and deterministic replay. Tasks were deterministically generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and carry structured difficulty metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, pattern, required_command_count, level ∈ {medium, hard, very_hard}). The preregistration required deterministic three‑replay consistency checks for each agent+simulator pair; pairs failing deterministic replay or encountering simulator errors would be excluded per the missingness_plan. In this execution all three‑replay checks passed and no exclusions were applied (complete_pairs = 400).

Confirmatory and secondary procedures. Primary analysis used an exact permutation on paired safe‑deploy booleans; McNemar provided corroboration. Secondary outcomes included bootstrap CI for median time‑to‑rollback and counts of repair attempts. Sensitivity analyses (treat excluded pairs as failures, restricted permutations) were preregistered but unnecessary here because no exclusions occurred. All seeds, analysis code, and logs are archived.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and reconciliation. Run start: 2026‑08‑29T18:23:37Z; completion: 2026‑08‑29T19:12:38Z. Planned episodes = 800; completed episodes = 800; failed episodes = 0; model_calls_used = 400 (shared initial generation); complete_pairs = 400. Deterministic three‑replay checks passed for all pairs; exclusions = 0.

Primary confirmatory outcomes (artifact‑grounded). The archived analysis artifacts report baseline_success_count = 400 (baseline_success_rate = 1.0) and guarded_success_count = 400 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency: n_11 = 400; n_10 = 0; n_01 = 0; n_00 = 0. Observed paired difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.0. The preregistered permutation test returned p = 1.0; exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.0] (bootstrap_seed = 1729; 10,000 resamples). Cohen's h = 0.0. These numbers are reproduced directly from the archived analysis artifacts (analysis/*).

Repair and rollback observations. Across the 800 episodes repair_applied = false and no rollbacks were invoked; validator_trace entries show validation_after.final_state matched expected_final_state for accepted configurations. Because the shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5, both baseline and guarded episodes necessarily recorded safe‑deploy outcomes for every pair.

Representative worked example (artifact‑grounded). Pair pair‑000001 (task_id = task‑000001; generation_seed = 1) illustrates the flow. The shared LLM candidate (stored at execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt) produced the canonical 4‑line configuration: interface edge1 admin down; interface edge1 vlan 30; interface edge1 mtu 1600; interface edge1 admin up. The validator_trace for both episodes records valid = true, parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, repair_applied = false, and final_state matching the task manifest's expected_final_state. The raw response and validator traces for this pair are archived and reproduced among the artifact examples.

Difficulty metadata and diversity. Each task manifest entry contains a difficulty label; the representative sample of the first six archived tasks contains 1 medium, 2 hard, and 3 very_hard entries (see execution/task_manifest.jsonl). Full per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 tasks are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl for auditors to aggregate deterministically; we do not invent aggregated totals beyond the archived representative examples.
sections.discussion:
Why the primary estimand became uninformative. Two preregistered design choices produced the deterministic ceiling. First, shared_initial_generation removed generator variance by delivering identical LLM outputs to baseline and guarded episodes. Second, the runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer were the same deterministic implementation (deterministic_netops_validator_v5). When deterministic_netops_validator_v5 accepts the shared candidate, both conditions record identical safe‑deploy outcomes and the paired difference must be zero. This outcome is a construct‑validity consequence of the frozen design rather than a general null statement about verifier utility across diverse generator/validator pairings.

Consequences for power and inference. The preregistered power calculation assumed within‑pair variability sufficient to detect an absolute difference of ≈0.10 with N=400; those assumptions are violated by the observed deterministic ceiling and therefore the original power rationale does not apply. Exact p‑values of 1.0 correctly reflect the observed data but provide no evidence about whether a runtime guard would improve outcomes under an alternative design that preserves generator variance.

Artifact‑grounded benchmark hardening recommendations. From archived validator_trace and execution accounting we derive concrete, artifact‑implementable steps to preserve signal in future confirmatory runs:

1) Independent per‑condition generation (independent_condition_generation = true) so each condition receives independently sampled generator outputs and the guard has bona fide opportunities to accept, block, or request repair.

2) Distinct runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer (or a held‑out scorer) to avoid conflating runtime acceptance with analysis scoring; archived validator_trace entries show acceptance decisions and validation_before/after states—using a separate scorer preserves adjudication.

3) Controlled adversarial seeding: preregister a reproducible fraction of perturbation seeds expected to produce baseline failures; the deterministic task generator supports seed injection for reproducible adversarial examples.

4) Difficulty‑stratified sampling: ensure the benchmark composition contains a sufficient proportion of tasks labeled very_hard to produce measurable baseline errors; per‑task difficulty labels are archived and can be sampled deterministically.

5) Instrumented mitigation metrics: enable and record repair attempts, repairs applied, and time‑to‑rollback as preregistered secondary outcomes (these fields are already present in validator_trace entries and repair logs in the artifact bundle).

Operational implication. For practitioners: experiment designs that remove generation variance can hide potential guard benefits; independent adjudication channels (distinct scorers or human reviewers) are important for measuring guard impact. Benchmarks intended to validate runtime safety mechanisms should preserve signal for guard interventions by incorporating independent generation, adversarial perturbations, or heterogeneous validators.
sections.conclusion: We ran a fully preregistered paired evaluation comparing a verifier‑augmented NetOps pipeline to an LLM‑only pipeline on an action‑aware staging benchmark. Under the preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator pairing, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and both conditions produced 100% safe‑deploy across N=400 pairs (paired difference = 0.0; permutation p = 1.0). The deterministic ceiling is a valid, artifact‑grounded outcome of the preregistered design and renders the primary estimand uninformative for generator×guard closed‑loop interactions in this run. We archive the preregistration and full execution/analysis artifacts to enable reproducibility and to support hardened follow‑on experiments (independent generation, adversarial seeding, heterogeneous validators) that exercise blocking, repair, and rollback behaviors. The artifact‑grounded hardening recommendations above give concrete steps researchers can preregister to preserve statistical signal when evaluating runtime verifier utility in NetOps settings.

Runtime guard and post‑hoc scorer: deterministic_netops_validator_v5. Task generator: deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5. Topic constraints were selected pre‑lock by the Research Director and limited the study to Generative AI and LLMs for NetOps focused on reliability/safety of intent→configuration generation. limitations: Benchmark hardness and ceiling effect: under preregistered shared_initial_generation semantics and the chosen generator+validator, every shared candidate satisfied deterministic_netops_validator_v5 so the guard had no opportunity to alter outcomes; this makes the primary estimand effectively untestable in this run and invalidates the original power rationale.

Model and scope: the experiment used a single generator (gpt-5-mini) and a single deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5); results do not generalize across models, validators, or production heterogeneity.

Construct validity: the same deterministic_netops_validator_v5 implementation served as both runtime guard and the post‑hoc scorer; this conflation produces concordant acceptance/scoring and limits inference about independent closed‑loop verifier utility.

Shared candidate semantics: preregistered shared_initial_generation (one LLM generation per task shared by both conditions) intentionally reduces generation variance and therefore limits inference to the validator’s behavior on identical candidates rather than full generator+guard closed‑loop interactions.

Synthetic environment and external validity: the simulator and validator do not fully model production telemetry noise, operator workflows, or adversarial actor behaviours; external validity to live networks is limited.

Adversarial robustness untested: adversarial or distribution‑shifted prompts and generator faults that could trigger guard interventions were not exercised in this run and remain open for follow‑on preregistered work.

Aggregated difficulty reporting: full per‑task difficulty labels for all N=400 are archived in execution/task_manifest.jsonl and can be aggregated by auditors; this manuscript reports representative sample counts to illustrate benchmark diversity but does not invent aggregated totals absent an explicit artifact summary included here.
